title: An isolated fibre point becomes a finite piece after an elementary etale base change
statement: Let $f:X\to S$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme] which is locally of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], let $x\in X$ and $s=f(x)$, and assume that $x$ is an isolated point of the fibre $X_s=X\times_S\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)$ [def-pc-scheme-fibre] (the singleton $\{x\}$ is open in $X_s$). Then there are a scheme $U$, an etale morphism $\varphi:U\to S$ [def-weil-etale-morphism] and a point $u\in U$ with $\varphi(u)=s$ such that the map $\kappa(s)\to\kappa(u)$ induced by $\varphi$ on residue fields [def-weil-residue-field] is an isomorphism (an elementary etale neighbourhood of $(S,s)$), and an open subscheme $V$ of the fibre product $X_U=X\times_SU$ [def-pc-fibre-product], with projections $p:X_U\to X$ and $q:X_U\to U$, such that: (i) the composite $V\hookrightarrow X_U\xrightarrow{q}U$ is finite [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]; (ii) there is exactly one point $v\in V$ with $q(v)=u$; (iii) $p(v)=x$, and the map $\kappa(x)\to\kappa(v)$ induced by $p$ is an isomorphism.

source.place: More on Morphisms, Lemma 02LK (more-morphisms-lemma-etale-makes-quasi-finite-finite-at-point, lines 11924-11967), statement (a), (b), (i)-(iii) and proof (reduction to affine opens $x\in Y\subseteq X$, $f(Y)\subseteq W\subseteq S$, then Algebra, Lemma 00UJ, algebra-lemma-etale-makes-quasi-finite-finite-one-prime). The final assertion of 02LK (persistence under a further elementary etale neighbourhood) is the separate node lem-weil-pbc-elementary-etale-finite-piece-persistence, stated there for any triple with (i)-(iii).

proof.text: Affine opens and the ring map (Stacks: 'Let $Y\subset X$, $W\subset S$ be affine opens such that $f(Y)\subset W$ and such that $x\in Y$'). Every point of a scheme has an affine open neighbourhood [def-pc-scheme]: choose an affine open $W\subseteq S$ with $s\in W$, and then, in the open subscheme $f^{-1}(W)$ of $X$, an affine open $Y$ with $x\in Y$, so $f(Y)\subseteq W$. Put $R=\mathcal O_S(W)$ and $A=\mathcal O_X(Y)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-spec-points] there are open immersions $\iota_W:\operatorname{Spec}R\to S$, $\iota_Y:\operatorname{Spec}A\to X$ [def-weil-open-immersion] with images $W$ and $Y$, and primes $\mathfrak p\subset R$, $\mathfrak q\subset A$ with $\iota_W(\mathfrak p)=s$, $\iota_Y(\mathfrak q)=x$. Since $f\circ\iota_Y$ has image in $W$ and $\iota_W$ is an isomorphism onto the open subscheme $W$, $f\circ\iota_Y=\iota_W\circ g$ for a unique morphism $g:\operatorname{Spec}A\to\operatorname{Spec}R$, and $g=\operatorname{Spec}\varphi$ for exactly one ring map $\varphi:R\to A$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum], namely the map $\mathcal O_S(W)\to\mathcal O_X(Y)$ induced by $f$; $\operatorname{Spec}\varphi$ sends a prime $\mathfrak Q$ to $\varphi^{-1}(\mathfrak Q)$. As $f$ is locally of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], $\varphi$ is of finite type by [lem-weil-pbc-lft-affine-pairs]. Finally $\iota_W(\varphi^{-1}(\mathfrak q))=f(\iota_Y(\mathfrak q))=f(x)=s=\iota_W(\mathfrak p)$ and $\iota_W$ is injective, so $\varphi^{-1}(\mathfrak q)=\mathfrak p$.

$\mathfrak q$ is isolated over $\mathfrak p$ (Stacks: 'Note that $x$ is also an isolated point of the fibre of the morphism $f|_Y:Y\to W$'). By [def-pc-scheme-fibre] the first projection $X_s\to X$ is a homeomorphism onto the subspace $f^{-1}(s)$, so the hypothesis says that $\{x\}$ is open in $f^{-1}(s)$. Since $Y\cap f^{-1}(s)$ is an open subset of $f^{-1}(s)$ containing $x$, $\{x\}$ is open in the subspace $Y\cap f^{-1}(s)$. The open immersion $\iota_Y$ is a homeomorphism of $\operatorname{Spec}A$ onto $Y$ [def-weil-open-immersion], and for $\mathfrak Q\in\operatorname{Spec}A$ we have $f(\iota_Y(\mathfrak Q))=\iota_W(\varphi^{-1}(\mathfrak Q))$, which equals $s=\iota_W(\mathfrak p)$ iff $\varphi^{-1}(\mathfrak Q)=\mathfrak p$ (step 1, $\iota_W$ injective). So $\iota_Y$ restricts to a homeomorphism from the subspace $P=\{\mathfrak Q\in\operatorname{Spec}A:\varphi^{-1}(\mathfrak Q)=\mathfrak p\}$ onto $Y\cap f^{-1}(s)$, sending $\mathfrak q$ to $x$; hence $\mathfrak q$ is an isolated point of $P$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. In Lean this is implemented by Scheme.Hom.quasiFiniteAt_iff_isOpen_singleton_asFiber followed by Scheme.Hom.QuasiFiniteAt.quasiFiniteAt on the chosen affine pair; no separatedness hypothesis is required.

The algebra case (Stacks: 'Hence we reduce to the case where $f$ is a morphism of affine schemes. This case is Algebra, Lemma 00UJ'). By steps 1 and 2, [lem-weil-pbc-etale-quasi-finite-finite-one-prime] applies to $\varphi:R\to A$ and $\mathfrak q$: there are an etale ring map $\psi:R\to R'$ with $\operatorname{Spec}\psi$ etale [def-weil-etale-morphism], a prime $\mathfrak p'\subset R'$ with $\psi^{-1}(\mathfrak p')=\mathfrak p$ and $\kappa(\mathfrak p)\to\kappa(\mathfrak p')$ an isomorphism, an idempotent $e\in C=R'\otimes_RA$ with $C_e$ a finite $R'$-module [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime], and a prime $\mathfrak r\subset C$ lying over $\mathfrak p'$ with $e\notin\mathfrak r$, the only prime of $C$ lying over $\mathfrak p'$ and not containing $e$, whose preimage under $a\mapsto1\otimes a$ is $\mathfrak q$.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma 00UJ (algebra-lemma-etale-makes-quasi-finite-finite-one-prime, line 40228), applied as in More on Morphisms 02LK, proof, line 11964

proof.text: The elementary etale neighbourhood (a) (written out by the agent). Put $U=\operatorname{Spec}R'$, $u=\mathfrak p'\in U$ and $\phi=\iota_W\circ\operatorname{Spec}\psi:U\to S$. The morphism $\operatorname{Spec}\psi$ is etale (step 3; [lem-weil-pbc-etale-ring-map-iff-etale-affine] for the equivalence with Algebra, Definition 00U1), the open immersion $\iota_W$ is etale by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation] (1), so $\phi$ is etale by (2) [def-weil-etale-morphism]. Also $\phi(u)=\iota_W(\psi^{-1}(\mathfrak p'))=\iota_W(\mathfrak p)=s$. Residue fields: $\iota_W$ is an isomorphism onto the open subscheme $W$, so it induces an isomorphism of local rings $\mathcal O_{S,s}\cong\mathcal O_{\operatorname{Spec}R,\mathfrak p}$ and of residue fields [def-weil-residue-field]; by [lem-weil-pbc-spec-residue-field-identification] the residue fields of $\operatorname{Spec}R$ at $\mathfrak p$ and of $\operatorname{Spec}R'$ at $\mathfrak p'$ are identified with $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$, $\kappa(\mathfrak p')$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime] compatibly with the maps from $R$, $R'$; the map induced by $\operatorname{Spec}\psi$ on residue fields then corresponds to the field map $\kappa(\mathfrak p)\to\kappa(\mathfrak p')$ induced by $\psi$, since both are field maps agreeing on the image of $R$ (the map of stalks of $\operatorname{Spec}\psi$ is $R_{\mathfrak p}\to R'_{\mathfrak p'}$ composed with the germ maps) and $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ is generated as a field by the image of $R$. As $\kappa(\mathfrak p)\to\kappa(\mathfrak p')$ is an isomorphism (step 3), $\kappa(s)\to\kappa(u)$ induced by $\phi$ is an isomorphism: $(U,u)\to(S,s)$ is an elementary etale neighbourhood. The private Lean helper spec_residueFieldMap_conjugate specializes [lem-weil-pbc-spec-map-residue-field-naturality] by composing with the inverse affine residue-field identification, so the bijectivity from 00UJ gives an isomorphism of scheme residue fields.

proof.text: The open $V$ (b) (Stacks: 'If we can prove the theorem for $f|_Y:Y\to W$, then the theorem follows for $f$'; written out by the agent). Let $X_U=X\times_SU$ with projections $p:X_U\to X$, $q:X_U\to U$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-open-fibre-product] to $f$ and $\phi$ with the open subschemes $W\subseteq S$, $Y\subseteq X$, $U\subseteq U$ ($f(Y)\subseteq W$, $\phi(U)\subseteq W$): $Y\times_WU\to X_U$ is an open immersion onto $p^{-1}(Y)$, compatible with the projections. Identifying $Y\cong\operatorname{Spec}A$ and $W\cong\operatorname{Spec}R$ by $\iota_Y$, $\iota_W$ (step 1), under which $f|_Y$ and $U\to W$ become $\operatorname{Spec}\varphi$ and $\operatorname{Spec}\psi$, [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra] gives $Y\times_WU\cong\operatorname{Spec}(A\otimes_RR')\cong\operatorname{Spec}C$ (swapping the factors), with the projections $\operatorname{Spec}$ of $A\to C$, $a\mapsto1\otimes a$, and of $R'\to C$, $r'\mapsto r'\otimes1$. So there is an open immersion $j:\operatorname{Spec}C\to X_U$ [def-weil-open-immersion] with $p\circ j=\iota_Y\circ\operatorname{Spec}(a\mapsto1\otimes a)$ and $q\circ j=\operatorname{Spec}(r'\mapsto r'\otimes1)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-principal-localization-open-immersion] the morphism $\operatorname{Spec}C_e\to\operatorname{Spec}C$ is an open immersion with image $D(e)=\{\mathfrak Q:e\notin\mathfrak Q\}$. Let $V=j(D(e))$, an open subscheme of $X_U$; then $k:\operatorname{Spec}C_e\to\operatorname{Spec}C\xrightarrow{j}X_U$ is an isomorphism onto $V$ and $q\circ k=\operatorname{Spec}(R'\to C_e)$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum].

proof.text: (i) $V\to U$ is finite (written out by the agent). By step 5 the composite $V\hookrightarrow X_U\xrightarrow{q}U$ is isomorphic over $U$ to $\operatorname{Spec}(R'\to C_e):\operatorname{Spec}C_e\to\operatorname{Spec}R'=U$. Cover $U$ by the single affine open $U$; its preimage $V\cong\operatorname{Spec}C_e$ is affine and the induced ring map $\mathcal O_U(U)=R'\to\mathcal O_V(V)=C_e$ is $R'\to C_e$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum], which is finite by step 3. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-local-on-target] (2)$\Rightarrow$(1), $V\to U$ is finite [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]. The Lean proof identifies Spec C_e with its open image using Scheme.Hom.isoOpensRange and transfers IsFinite across that isomorphism; IsFinite.SpecMap_iff and the module-finiteness supplied by 00UJ prove finiteness of the affine spectrum map.

proof.text: (ii) and the first half of (iii) (written out by the agent). Every point of $V$ is $k(\mathfrak Q')$ for a unique prime $\mathfrak Q'$ of $C_e$, i.e. $j(\mathfrak Q)$ for a unique prime $\mathfrak Q$ of $C$ with $e\notin\mathfrak Q$ (step 5), and $q(j(\mathfrak Q))$ is the preimage of $\mathfrak Q$ under $R'\to C$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. So the points $v\in V$ with $q(v)=u=\mathfrak p'$ correspond to the primes of $C$ lying over $\mathfrak p'$ not containing $e$; by step 3 there is exactly one, $\mathfrak r$. Put $v=j(\mathfrak r)$: it is the unique point of $V$ over $u$. Further $p(v)=\iota_Y(\mathfrak r')$ where $\mathfrak r'$ is the preimage of $\mathfrak r$ under $a\mapsto1\otimes a$, which is $\mathfrak q$ by step 3; so $p(v)=\iota_Y(\mathfrak q)=x$.

proof.text: Residue fields in (iii). Let z be the image of v in X_U and let T be the canonical pushout of the residue fields at its two projections over their common base residue field [def-pc-fibre-product, def-weil-residue-field]. Since the second base residue-field map is an isomorphism by step 4, the first pushout inclusion kappa(p(z)) -> T is an isomorphism. Thus T is a field. The canonical map ofPointTensor z from T to kappa(z) is injective because it is a field homomorphism, so its kernel is zero and the quotient by the kernel is again a field. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-point-residue-field] to get a ring equivalence from that quotient to kappa(z), compatible with the first inclusion. The quotient map is surjective, the first inclusion is bijective, and the equivalence is surjective. Their composite is the first projection's residue-field map, which is therefore surjective; it is injective as a map of fields. Finally the open inclusion V -> X_U induces a residue-field isomorphism, and functoriality of residueFieldMap gives the assertion at v. This uses the canonical tensor map at the already constructed point, and does not use classification of fibre-product points by primes.

lean.statement: theorem exists_etale_finite_open_of_isolated_fiber_point {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) [LocallyOfFiniteType f] (x : X) (hx : IsOpen ({f.asFiber x} : Set (f.fiber (f x)))) : ∃ (U : Scheme.{u}) (φ : U ⟶ S) (u : U), Etale φ ∧ φ u = f x ∧ IsIso (φ.residueFieldMap u) ∧ ∃ (V : (pullback f φ).Opens), IsFinite (V.ι ≫ pullback.snd f φ) ∧ ∃ (v : V), (V.ι ≫ pullback.snd f φ) v = u ∧ (∀ (w : V), (V.ι ≫ pullback.snd f φ) w = u → w = v) ∧ (V.ι ≫ pullback.fst f φ) v = x ∧ IsIso ((V.ι ≫ pullback.fst f φ).residueFieldMap v)
